name: Opus Picks-and-Shovels
strategy: An AI-buildout memory-bottleneck book re-entered at reduced size: a single 25% Micron (DRAM/HBM) leg bought back about 30% below its late-October high after the post-midterm memory rout, with 75% in cash at 4% APY until the policy overhang and the memory-pricing trend settle.
reassessment_note: Both legs stopped out on 2026-11-05 (MU at 656.39, -27%; SNDK at 806.43, -36%), so the book was 100% cash. Research (Yahoo closes plus 24/7 Wall St, INDmoney, Benzinga and TrendForce coverage; several pages were 403-blocked) shows the 11-04/11-05 rout was mainly political. Democrats took both chambers on 11-03, Rep. Ansari called for an AI pause, and Democratic messaging wants data centers to pay their own power and grid costs, on top of Texas's existing data-center permitting pause. Fundamentals have not broken. Micron says more than 75% of FY27 shipments are committed and it has no line of sight to supply/demand balance. TrendForce's October report has server and PC DRAM contract prices still rising. A federal AI pause also cannot become law past a presidential veto. Against that, contract-price gains are narrowing, spot prices have retreated, and the tape (SMH -14% from 10-29 to 11-05, only a partial bounce on 11-06) is in a regime that can keep hitting stops. So I am not rebuilding the old 57% memory book. I am re-entering only the highest-quality bottleneck name, MU, at 25%, with a stop set wider than the daily volatility, and holding the rest in cash. SNDK is not re-bought: NAND has less contract cover and was the bigger loser. Lesson recorded: the prior book was too large in a name that can move 17% in a day.

positions.thesis: Micron closed 690.00 on 11-06, about 30% below the 983 close on 10-28. A political shock (Democratic midterm sweep, AI-pause rhetoric, data-center power-cost proposals) erased demand that is largely already contracted: more than 75% of FY27 shipments are committed, and HBM/server DRAM contract prices were still rising in TrendForce's October read. Legislation that would actually curb US AI capex faces a veto, and hyperscalers can site capacity abroad. Size is 25%, not 45%, because spot prices are rolling over, contract gains are narrowing, and the stock just gapped 17% in a day. A 20% stop (about 552) sits below the 11-05 low with room for normal volatility and caps the loss at about 5% of NAV. A 45% take-profit (about 1000) is roughly a retest of the late-October highs if the policy fear fades into Nvidia's late-November print.
